title: What is the balance after three credits and three debits?
description: An account starts with nothing in it. Credits of thirty, forty and fifty rupees come in, and debits of forty, fifty and sixty rupees go out. The credits and the debits are added up separately, and the balance is found.
teaching_notes: One idea: add all the credits, add all the debits, and take the debits away from the credits. Watch for students who say the balance cannot go below zero.

video_script.why: The child finds a balance from many credits and debits by totalling each kind and taking one total away from the other.
video_script.substitution: Add the credits, add the debits, and take the debits away from the credits; a bigger debit total leaves a negative balance.
video_script.payoff_line: The balance is negative thirty rupees.
maths_rules: check by running balance: 30, 70, 120, 80, 30, then the last debit of 60 takes it to −30
video_script.design: One passbook with six entries. The credits are totalled, the debits are totalled, and the debits are taken away from the credits. The check runs through the six entries one at a time.
